narrative:
The model estimated a 78% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, which is why your law school application was denied. This is a strong risk estimate, not a verdict on your ability, and it means the decision treated first-time bar success as unlikely based on your academic profile. Your gender and race were not used in this prediction.

The strongest factor was your third-year class-rank decile. You were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA was the next most influential factor, but it worked in your favor: at 3.10 it is only slightly below the accepted-student average of 3.23, so it modestly pushed toward passing. Your LSAT score was the third most important factor and pushed toward failure: a 26 is well below the accepted average of about 37. Your low first-year rank also aligns with the concern, though it ranked below these three drivers.

To move forward, ask admissions for specific feedback and consider retaking the LSAT after structured preparation. Strengthen your record with recent rigorous coursework or a graduate-level program that demonstrates academic readiness, especially if it addresses your third-year rank. Reapply when you can show improved test performance and a stronger recent academic trend, and discuss your bar-readiness plan with an advisor.
